items.title: ‘Mogging’ is Collins’ word of the year, but what does it mean?
items.brief: “Mogging,” a tongue-in-cheek term jovially used by members of Gen-Z and Gen Alpha to suggest an outperforming or outshining of someone or something, has been crowned 2026’s word of the year by Collins English Dictionary.

items.title: At least 31 dead after Russia drops nine bombs on a Ukrainian school building
items.brief: Dozens of people were killed when Russia dropped at least nine bombs on a school building in southeastern Ukraine where they had taken shelter.

items.title: A West Point cadet drugged his girlfriend to force an unwanted abortion. Then he graduated from Cornell
items.brief: A onetime West Point cadet drugged his then-girlfriend in her barracks room, administered abortion pills to her against her will and caused a miscarriage.

items.title: Spanish soccer player Jesús de Miguel dies after on-pitch collision
items.brief: Soccer player Jesús de Miguel has died after an on-field collision during a Spanish second-division match on Monday, his club CD Tenerife has said.

items.title: Child in New York dies after contracting measles, the state’s first such death in 30 years
items.brief: A child in Lewis County, New York, has died after contracting measles, officials announced Monday.

items.title: An hour-by-hour guide to election night poll closings
items.brief: It’s Election Day, and the balance of power in Washington is at stake as Americans vote to determine control of the Senate and House of Representatives — plus, settle races for governor and decide many other key issues.

items.title: US military conducts strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island in defensive operation, officials say
items.brief: The US military carried out limited strikes on Iran’s Qeshm Island on Monday, three US officials told CNN, characterizing the action as defensive in nature and meant to protect US assets in the region.
